answer: An AI-agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using proof-of-inference challenges. To establish an identity, an agent must submit verifiable compute traces for non-cacheable tasks, like analyzing meter in a sonnet or classifying scans of a walnut. This burns scarce GPU cycles and electricity per identity, preventing credentials from persisting as a free relic. However, wealthy adversaries with massive compute clusters can still mass-produce identities.
